 Introduction
These sample schemes of work and lesson plans for English and Kiswahili Grades 1, 2 and 3, have been developed by the Tusome team to guide teachers to create their own. They
provide detailed week by week and day by day example activities that can be used to teach learners using Tusome materials, while ensuring that the teachers follow the new
curriculum designs developed by the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD).
The schemes of work and lesson plans have been developed based on templates provided by the KICD and contain all the components of the Competence Based Curriculum
designs.
Key areas highlighted in the sample schemes of work and lesson plans include the following:
 These are the general topics and sub topics of each learning area in the KICD Curriculum Designs. They give the specific skills and sub
 skills that learners should attain at the end of a lesson. The teacher should ensure that each lesson has a reference to a sub strand and
Strand/Substrand strand picked from the curriculum designs. In English and Kiswahili language, the four main skills, listening, speaking, reading and
 writing are covered as strands. Since skills build on each other, these four strands should not be taught in isolation. Tusome ensures that
 all these strands are covered in each lesson.
Specific Learning The Competence Based Curriculum has moved from objective based learning to outcome based learning. The teacher is expected to list
Outcomes down what will be achieved at the end of each lesson. Learning outcomes focus on learner’s achievement rather than what the teacher
 is expected to teach.
Key Inquiry These are the questions that will guide the teachers as they teach. These questions are meant to help with learning and are not a form
Questions of assessment. Key inquiry questions should enhance inquiry learning where learners and the teacher engage in discussions to achieve
 learning outcomes.
 A core competence refers to the ability to apply appropriate knowledge, skill and attitude to perform a function successfully. The
Core Competencies seven core competencies to be achieved by every learner in basic education are: communication and collaboration, selfefficacy, critical
 thinking and problem solving, creativity and imagination, citizenship, digital literacy and learning to learn.
 Values are principles or morals obligations. They make one of the key pillars of basic education. Education should promote acquisition
Values: of national values as enshrined in the Kenya Constitution. It should be geared towards developing a selfdisciplined and ethical citizen
 with sound moral and religious values.
Pertinent and The Competence Based Curriculum ensures that pertinent and contemporary issues (PCIS) facing the society form part of the
 curriculum.
Contemporary issues technological,PCIs are society challenges experienced as a result of dynamism in various aspects of the society ranging from social,
(PCIs) economic, and cultural changes. There are 6 main PCIs covered in the Competence Based Curriculum include citizenship,
 health education, life skills and values education, nonformal programs and community service and parental engagement.
Sample lesson plans
The sample lesson plans are divided into four main areas:
Introduction: During introduction, the teacher is expected to review previous lessons. They should state the objective of the lesson and link this lesson to previous lesson.
Introduction should be captivating and should elicit learner’s interest.
1. Lesson Development: During lesson development, the teacher provides content of the lesson. Lesson development involve taking the learners carefully through every step
 to ensure that they are able to achieve the learning outcomes anticipated at the end of the lesson.
2. Conclusion: During conclusion, the teacher assesses if learners have gained from the lesson. It is also the time that learners are given an opportunity to ask questions and
 given classwork and homework.
3. Summary: The summary highlights the key points in the lesson. It is a recap of the lesson.
 Teachers are expected to closely study the sample schemes of work and lesson plans and then using the Tusome materials and other resources create their own schemes of
 work and lesson plans.

SCHOOL GRADE LEARNING AREA DATE TIME ROLL
 3 English Language Activities
Strand: Listening, speaking, reading, writing (Activities at home and at school)
Sub-strand: Listening, pronunciation, language structures and functions, word and text reading, fluency;
comprehension, handwriting
Specific Learning Outcomes
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. explain meaning of vocabulary; ‘block’, ‘bring’, ‘able’ for self-expression
2. construct meaningful sentences using the vocabulary in variety of contexts
3. read and answer question on the text, ‘Kobe’s new school’ for comprehension
4. use verbs correctly to show singular and plural subjects for effective communication.
Key Inquiry Questions
1. How do you sit while reading?
2. What do you see in the pictures?
3. What do you think will happen in the story?
Core competences: Communication and collaboration, creativity and imagination, critical thinking and problem
solving
Values: Sharing, love, responsibility
PCIs: Education for sustainable development (ESD); animal welfare appreciating wildlife and forests.
Learning Resources
Tusome English Teacher’s Guide page 1-2
Tusome English Pupil’s Book page 1-2
Flashcards/ word cards, pictures/diagrams
Organization of learning
Classroom: Pupils sitting in rows
 Introduction (Assessment as learning)
Guide learners to sing a song about a school then ask them to name the activities that they do at school.
 Lesson Development (Assessment as learning)
Step 1: Vocabulary
Guide learners to explain the vocabulary; block, bring and able using the Direct Instruction Model (DIM)
Step 2: Comprehension
Inquiry Question: How do you sit while reading?
1. Before Reading
 Guide learners to read and discuss the title, pictures and make prediction in pairs using DIM.
2. During Reading
 Guide learners to read the text, ‘Kobe’s new school using DIM.
3. After Reading
 Guide learners to answer question on the text using DIM.
Step 3: Grammar
Guide learners to make sentences using verbs that show singular and plural subjects using DIM
 Conclusion (Assessment as learning)
Ask learners to make their own sentences using the verbs that show singular and plural subjects.
Check the learners work. Allow learners to ask questions for clarification. Gives homework activity.
 Summary
Highlights key points of the lesson.
Extension Activities
Construct sentences based on the following words: block, bring, able and read to the parents at home.
Reflection/Self-remarks
